learning_outcomes: Understand behaviour change as a structured, staged process.
Recognise why harmful patterns persist in parenting and family dynamics.
Identify readiness, resistance, and ambivalence in behaviour change.
Apply evidence-based behaviour change strategies safely.
Support children and caregivers through sustainable, non-coercive change.

lesson_content.definition: Behaviour change is a gradual, structured process where individuals shift patterns of thinking, reacting, and relating. It requires safety, clarity, consistency, and support—not pressure or coercion.

behaviour_change_stages.description: Recognising that a behaviour is harmful or ineffective.
examples: Realising a child withdraws when shamed

behaviour_change_stages.description: Exploring why the behaviour occurs and what triggers it.
Deciding to change and committing to new patterns.
Trying new behaviours and adjusting when challenges arise.

video_lesson.title: How Behaviour Change Works
script: Behaviour change is not instant—it is a gradual, structured process.
Parents often repeat patterns because they are overwhelmed, stressed, or repeating what they learned growing up.
Real change begins with awareness, followed by understanding, intention, practice, and maintenance.
Children thrive when parents shift from reactive patterns to calm, connected responses.
This lesson teaches how to recognise readiness for change and build sustainable new behaviours.

activities.description: Sort behaviours into correct behaviour change stages.
Identify behaviour change stage and explain likely impacts.

scenarios.text: A parent realises their child becomes anxious when they raise their voice.
A parent practices pausing before responding during conflict.
